selected_evidence.summary: Captured RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64, XFS, source metadata, original `cat` utility, and compatible GNU coreutils 9.5.
Shows the installed `cp --sparse=always` implementation, root ownership, mode 0755, and valid shell syntax.

selected_evidence.requirement: Preserve logical length, bytes, holes, source integrity, and repeat safety
selected_evidence.summary: After two copies over an 80 MiB allocated destination, the result is 67,108,864 bytes logically, 8,192 bytes allocated, byte-identical, and SHA-256-identical. Source hash remained unchanged and same-file copying was safely refused.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep installed OS release and kernel
selected_evidence.summary: Pre- and post-restart evidence shows unchanged RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

Healthy baseline boot ID f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c was captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID 916c9c7d-70f7-4005-adf8-f6179fa1caaf observed, and full system/utility/data recovery verified. Post-restart copy still allocated only 8,192 bytes.

commands.command:
set -eu
cd /srv/legacy2/sparse-image-copy
old_mode=$(stat -c '%a' bin/copy-image)
old_uid=$(stat -c '%u' bin/copy-image)
old_gid=$(stat -c '%g' bin/copy-image)
tmp=$(mktemp ./bin/.copy-image.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
cat > "$tmp" <<'COPY_IMAGE_EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ "$#" -ne 2 ]; then
    printf 'Usage: %s SOURCE DESTINATION\n' "$0" >&2
    exit 64
fi

# GNU cp's explicit sparse mode preserves the logical byte stream while
# turning sufficiently long zero runs into holes. It also refuses a
# same-file copy before truncating the source.
exec cp --sparse=always -- "$1" "$2"
COPY_IMAGE_EOF
chown "$old_uid:$old_gid" "$tmp"
chmod "$old_mode" "$tmp"
mv -f -- "$tmp" bin/copy-image
trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM
printf 'INSTALLED\n'
stat -c 'path=%n size=%s mode=%a owner=%U:%G' bin/copy-image
sed -n '1,80p' bin/copy-image
printf 'SYNTAX\n'
sh -n bin/copy-image && echo valid
commands.stdout:
INSTALLED
path=bin/copy-image size=336 mode=755 owner=root:root
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ "$#" -ne 2 ]; then
    printf 'Usage: %s SOURCE DESTINATION\n' "$0" >&2
    exit 64
fi

# GNU cp's explicit sparse mode preserves the logical byte stream while
# turning sufficiently long zero runs into holes. It also refuses a
# same-file copy before truncating the source.
exec cp --sparse=always -- "$1" "$2"
SYNTAX
valid

commands.command:
set -eu
cd /srv/legacy2/sparse-image-copy
src_hash_before=$(sha256sum source.img | awk '{print $1}')
rm -f destination.img
fallocate -l 80M destination.img
printf 'PREEXISTING_DESTINATION\n'
stat -c 'size=%s blocks=%b allocated=%B' destination.img
./bin/copy-image source.img destination.img
./bin/copy-image source.img destination.img
src_hash_after=$(sha256sum source.img | awk '{print $1}')
dst_hash=$(sha256sum destination.img | awk '{print $1}')
src_size=$(stat -c '%s' source.img)
dst_size=$(stat -c '%s' destination.img)
dst_blocks=$(stat -c '%b' destination.img)
dst_alloc=$((dst_blocks * 512))
printf 'FINAL_STATS\n'
stat -c 'path=%n size=%s blocks=%b block_bytes=%B' source.img destination.img
printf 'ALLOCATED_BYTES=%s\n' "$dst_alloc"
printf 'BYTE_COMPARE\n'
cmp -s source.img destination.img && echo identical
printf 'HASHES\nsource_before=%s\nsource_after=%s\ndestination=%s\n' "$src_hash_before" "$src_hash_after" "$dst_hash"
[ "$src_size" -eq 67108864 ]
[ "$dst_size" -eq "$src_size" ]
[ "$dst_alloc" -lt 2097152 ]
[ "$src_hash_before" = "$src_hash_after" ]
[ "$src_hash_after" = "$dst_hash" ]
printf 'SAME_FILE_GUARD\n'
if ./bin/copy-image source.img source.img > /tmp/copy-image-same.out 2>&1; then
    echo 'unexpected same-file success' >&2
    rm -f /tmp/copy-image-same.out
    exit 1
else
    sed -n '1,2p' /tmp/copy-image-same.out
    echo refused-without-truncation
fi
rm -f /tmp/copy-image-same.out
[ "$(sha256sum source.img | awk '{print $1}')" = "$src_hash_before" ]
printf 'ASSERTIONS\nall-copy-assertions-passed\n'
